# try to integrate with bitbucket

Integrate with the Bitbucket API so that `git mirror` can create the mirror repository, not only register its remote. Today the command assumes a repository already exists at `git@bitbucket.org:<owner>/<name>`; for a new project the author still has to open Bitbucket, create it by hand and only then run the command. The candidate library named in the note is [ktrysmt/go-bitbucket](https://github.com/ktrysmt/go-bitbucket), which implies a Go implementation rather than curl in bash — consistent with the author's later note that the git helpers are better rewritten in Go inside maintainer.

The core expectation is that `git mirror` (no argument) creates `<owner>/<name>` on Bitbucket when it is missing and then adds or updates the `mirror` remote. The note does not settle the details an implementation has to decide: the visibility of the new repository, where the credentials come from (environment, keychain — not the repository), what happens when the repository already exists, and how a failed API call is kept from leaving a half-configured remote.
